title: Question 9
stem:
A thin rectangular slice of aluminium has sides of length $65\text{ mm}$, $50\text{ mm}$ and $0.10\text{ mm}$, as shown in Fig. 9.1.
Some of the corners of the slice are labelled.
A current $I$ of $3.8\text{ A}$ is normal to face RSXY of the slice.
In aluminium, the number of free electrons per unit volume is $6.0 \times 10^{28}\text{ m}^{-3}$.
A uniform magnetic field of magnetic flux density $B$ equal to $0.13\text{ T}$ is normal to face QRYZ of the aluminium slice in the direction from Q to P.
A Hall voltage $V_{\text{H}}$ is developed across the slice and is given by the expression
$$V_{\text{H}} = \frac{BI}{ntq}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Use Fig. 9.1 to state the magnitude of the distance $t$.

$t = \text{..................................................... mm}$
hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
walkthrough:

Step 2: **Apply Physics Criteria**

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**

$V_{\text{H}} = \text{..................................................... V}$
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
VH = (0.13 × 3.8) / (6.0 × 1028 × 0.10 × 10-3 × 1.60 × 10-19); = 5.1 × 10-7 V
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
